key_insight: This review maps medical vision-language models from contrastive alignment and generative systems to pixel grounding, mixture-of-experts, and reinforcement-learning-based reasoning.
clinical_relevance: Aligning medical images with clinical text could support image interpretation, report generation, and question answering while reducing reliance on manual annotations.
method: Reviews foundation models that learn from paired images and text.
Organizes medical vision-language architectures into a taxonomy.
Examines data, reliability, computational, and evaluation challenges.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a review rather than a clinical validation study and reports no dataset sizes or quantitative performance results.
watch_item: Hallucinated outputs and a lack of standardized, clinically grounded evaluation limit confidence in real-world deployment.
paper_title: Multimodal AI in Healthcare: Review of Vision-Language Foundation Models for Real-World Medical Applications
